newsitem.title: UK: Russian envoy takes a shine to British toilets.
newsitem.headline: Russian envoy takes a shine to British toilets.

text.p: Russia's departing ambassador said goodbye on Sunday with a paean to Britain's public lavatories, calling them the hallmark of the most civilised society on earth.
Anatoly Adamishin wrote in the Sunday Times that many outsiders found the British more hypocritical than lovable.
But he said he had become convinced during a three-year posting that Britain was an "enchanted" place of smiling, friendly people, albeit with a gift for telling white lies.
"In my view, in terms of civilisation, the British Isles are more advanced than anybody. Perhaps they have left the rest of mankind behind," Adamishin, who is returning to Moscow, wrote.
A leading U.S. news magazine recently extolled London as the coolest of capitals for its nightlife and culture, but Adamishin sang Britain's praise for catering to a more basic need.
"Where can you find a country with so many public toilets? And so well maintained, too. British lavatories are not just spotlessly clean, they are cosy," the ambassador wrote.
He said he had never seen anything like one central London lavatory that boasted tiled walls with mosaics.
"You may shrug it off. But when a man reaches a certain age, with its attendant disorders, he comes to appreciate an abundance of public toilets," Adamishin, 62, said.
